recognize_zh: 骨髓抽吸抹片幾乎被大型單核母細胞（monoblasts）佔滿：細胞核圓形、染色質細緻、可見核仁，細胞質豐富呈灰藍色且無 Auer 小體，符合急性單核母細胞白血病；本圖為骨髓而非皮膚切片。
features: Sheets of large blasts with abundant moderately basophilic grey-blue cytoplasm
Round to slightly oval nuclei with fine lacy chromatin
One or more distinct nucleoli in many cells
Low to moderate N:C ratio with occasional faint cytoplasmic granules
Rare residual neutrophils and erythroid precursors
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear is hypercellular and nearly replaced by large blasts with abundant grey-blue, moderately basophilic cytoplasm, round nuclei, delicate lacy chromatin and prominent nucleoli. Auer rods are not seen, and residual granulocytic and erythroid elements are markedly reduced. Although titled leukemia cutis, this image depicts the marrow rather than the skin lesion. Findings are consistent with acute monoblastic leukemia; nonspecific esterase cytochemistry and flow cytometry (CD14, CD64, CD11b, CD4) are recommended for confirmation.

ddx.vs: Myeloblasts have a higher N:C ratio, less abundant cytoplasm, may contain Auer rods and are MPO positive, whereas monoblasts are NSE positive with weak or absent MPO.
Plasmablasts show eccentric nuclei with a perinuclear hof and are CD138/CD38 bright, lacking monocytic markers.
Lymphoma cells often show deeply basophilic vacuolated cytoplasm and express B- or T-cell markers rather than CD14/CD64 and lysozyme.
